records.text: This was their number: thirty gold cooling vessels, a thousand silver cooling vessels, twenty-nine miscellaneous items;
records.prior_reason: The thirty gold cooling vessels, thousand silver vessels and twenty-nine miscellaneous items have no separately verified parallel breakdown; the different aggregate in 1:11 is not used to force an arithmetic reconciliation.

records.text: thirty gold kephphoure, two hundred silver ones, and a thousand other vessels.
records.prior_reason: The kephphoure and other-vessel breakdown is not repeated in the retained restoration memorandum, and no identity with a different inventory is asserted.

records.text: The sons of Basou: three hundred and twenty-three.
records.prior_reason: Basou with 323 is not securely identified as Besi with 324 solely from placement in the parallel family register; the candidate remains unresolved.

records.text: The sons of Iora: one hundred and twelve.
records.prior_reason: Iora with 112 is not securely identified as Ariph with 112 solely from a shared total and register position; the candidate remains unresolved.

records.text: The sons of Asem: two hundred and twenty-three.
records.prior_reason: Asem with 223 is not securely identified as Esam with 328 in a differently placed entry; the candidate remains unresolved.

records.text: The sons of Gaber: ninety-five.
records.prior_reason: Gaber with 95 is not securely identified as Gabaon with 95 solely from the shared total in this register section; the candidate remains unresolved.

records.text: The sons of Magebos: one hundred and fifty-six.
records.prior_reason: The Magebos entry with 156 has no verified counterpart in the compared Nehemiah register, and it is not attached to an adjacent differently named locality.

records.text: On day one of the seventh month they began offering whole burnt offerings to the Lord, though the Lord’s house had not been founded.
records.prior_reason: The first-day commencement before foundation work is a particular chronology notice; no independently sufficient connection beyond already treated daily sacrifices was retained for this unit.

records.text: Iesous and his sons and his brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, sons of Judah, stood over those doing the work in the house of God; also the sons of Enadad, their sons and their brothers the Levites.
records.prior_reason: The supervising Iesous, Kadmiel and Enadad groups have differing genealogical wording from other lists; the Iesous here is not automatically identified as the high priest merely by name.

records.text: The people could not distinguish the sound of the joyful signal from the sound of the people’s weeping, for the people cried out with a loud voice, and the sound was heard far away.
records.prior_reason: The indistinguishable noise of joy and weeping is specific to this ceremony; a generic loud-assembly parallel adds no sufficiently particular connection.

records.text: Those who oppressed Judah and Benjamin heard that the sons of the deportation were building a house for the Lord, God of Israel.
records.prior_reason: The opponents hearing about the temple is a narrative introduction; no independently sufficient connection is retained merely because other rebuilding projects also had opponents.

records.text: In the reign of Asoueros, at the beginning of his reign, they wrote a letter against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.
records.prior_reason: The Asoueros accusation is not identified with another royal letter or reign on the strength of a familiar transliteration alone.

records.text: In the days of Arthasastha, Tabeel, together with the rest of his fellow slaves, wrote in peace for Mithradates to Arthasastha king of the Persians. The tax collector wrote a document in Syrian, and it was interpreted.
records.prior_reason: The named writers and Syrian language notice have no separately verified matching document; Arthasastha is not used to collapse all Persian correspondence into one letter.

records.text: Raoum the baaltam and Samsai the scribe wrote one letter against Jerusalem to Arthasastha the king.
records.prior_reason: Raoum and Samsai introducing their letter are not identified with similarly named people in the return registers.

records.text: These things were decided by Raoum the baaltam, Samsai the scribe and the rest of our fellow slaves—the Dinaians, Apharsathachaians, Tarphallaians, Apharsaians, Archyaians, Babylonians and Sousanachaians, who are Elamites,
records.prior_reason: The administrative and population-name list has no verified exact matching list, and its unusual terms are not silently corrected from another edition.

records.text: This is the wording of the letter they sent him: “To Arthasastha the king: your servants, men beyond the river.
records.prior_reason: The generic letter address to Arthasastha is not a sufficient cross-reference to another royal salutation.

records.text: It is not permitted for us to look upon the king’s disgrace. Therefore we have sent and informed the king,
records.prior_reason: The writers' profession of loyalty and their motive for informing the king have no sufficiently particular target beyond the letter's own general accusation.

records.text: We therefore inform the king that if that city is built and its walls put in order, you will have no peace.”
records.prior_reason: The predicted loss of peace has no separately verified outcome here; it is not converted into proof that the builders actually intended rebellion.

records.text: The king sent peace to Raoum the baaltam, Samsai the scribe, their remaining fellow slaves living in Samaria and the others beyond the river, and he says:
records.prior_reason: The royal reply's addressees are part of this correspondence; a generic reply pattern does not provide a particular additional connection.

records.text: “The tax collector whom you sent to us was called before me.
records.prior_reason: The tax collector being summoned is a particular administrative action whose exact counterpart has not been established.

records.text: you are on your guard against allowing slackness in this matter, lest destruction increase to the harm of kings.”
records.prior_reason: The admonition to avoid slackness is already context for the concrete stop-work order, but has no independently sufficient separate target retained for this source unit.

records.text: They sent him a statement, and this is written in it: “To Darius the king: all peace.
records.prior_reason: The letter's peace greeting to Darius is a conventional salutation and does not establish the identity of another letter.

records.text: I have also issued a decision: for anyone who changes this word, a timber will be taken down from his house, and he will be raised upright and fastened upon it. His house will be dealt with according to me.
records.prior_reason: The decree specifies a timber taken from the offender's house and his fastening upon it; no independently verified passage establishes this exact prescribed punishment. Generic royal penalties are insufficient.

records.text: son of Samaria, son of Esria, son of Mareroth,
records.prior_reason: The compressed Samaria-Esria-Mareroth priestly ancestry has spelling and sequence differences from the separately read Chronicles comparison; exact person-by-person equivalence remains unresolved.

records.text: son of Zaraia, son of Saouia, son of Bokki,
records.prior_reason: The Zaraia-Saouia-Bokki sequence is not silently normalized to the separately read Zaraia-Ozi-Bokai line; the middle name and exact ancestral equivalences remain unresolved.

records.text: “Arthasastha, king of kings, to Esdras, scribe of the law of the God of heaven: The word and the answer are completed.
records.prior_reason: The royal salutation identifies Ezra as scribe of the law of the God of heaven. Repeating that office later within the same decree provides no sufficiently meaningful connection beyond identification; no stronger particular target is retained in this pass.

records.text: He has been sent from the king and the seven advisers to inspect Judea and Jerusalem by the law of their God that is in your hand,
records.prior_reason: The commission from the king and seven advisers is read in context, but no specific independent inspection mission or adviser identities are established.

records.text: Whatever seems good to you and your brothers to do with the remaining silver and gold, do as is pleasing to your God.
records.prior_reason: The discretionary use of remaining funds has no specific reported decision in the texts read. The initial custody-of-offerings link was removed because custody does not establish how the remainder was used.

records.text: It has also been made known to you: from any priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, Nathinim or ministers of this house of God, let there be no tax for you; you shall have no authority to enslave them.
records.prior_reason: The exemption of temple service personnel from taxation and enslavement has no additional specifically verified counterpart selected in this pass; their shared occupational titles alone are insufficient.

records.text: from the sons of Zathoes, Sechenias son of Aziel, and with him three hundred males;
records.prior_reason: Zathoes is not silently equated with the sons of Zathoua in the separately read earlier list; the exact family-name correspondence remains unresolved.

records.text: from the sons of Elam, Iesia son of Athelia, and with him seventy males;
records.prior_reason: Elam is not automatically assigned to the earlier Ailam rather than Elam-ar entry; the separately read family-name candidate remains unresolved.

records.text: from the sons of Ioab, Abadia son of Iiel, and with him two hundred and eighteen males;
records.prior_reason: The sons of Ioab are not automatically identified with the Ioab subgroup within the earlier Phaathmoab entry; the precise relationship remains unresolved.

records.text: from the sons of Baani, Salimouth son of Iosephia, and with him one hundred and sixty males;
records.prior_reason: Baani is not silently changed to Banoui to force a family identification with the earlier return list.

records.text: From the sons of Bago, Outhi, and with him seventy males.
records.prior_reason: Bago is not silently normalized to Bagoi in the earlier return list; the exact family correspondence remains an unresolved candidate.

records.text: Only Ionathan son of Asael and Iazia son of Thekoue were with me concerning this, and Mesoulam and Sabathai the Levite were helping them.
records.prior_reason: The source says the named men were with Ezra and that others helped them. It is not rewritten as opposition to the reform, and their personal identities are not inferred from names alone.

records.text: From the sons of Eram: Masaia, Elia, Samaia, Iiel and Ozia.
records.prior_reason: The priestly sons of Eram are not silently equated with the earlier Erem entry or with the non-priestly Eram family; the separately read priestly-family comparison remains unresolved.

records.text: From the Levites: Iozabad, Samou, Kolia—he is Kolitas—Phathaia, Iodom and Eliezer.
records.prior_reason: The Levite Iozabad is not identified with Iozabad son of Iesous solely from name and office; the other names likewise lack independently established identities.

records.text: From the singers: Elisaph. From the gatekeepers: Sellem, Telem and Odoue.
records.prior_reason: The singer and gatekeeper names do not by themselves identify those individuals with ancestral service-family names in the earlier list.

records.text: From the sons of Elam: Mathania, Zacharia, Iaiel, Abdia, Iarimoth and Elia.
records.prior_reason: The sons of Elam are not assigned automatically to Ailam or Elam-ar in the earlier inventory; the individual listed men also lack established personal identifications.

records.text: Benjamin, Malouch and Samaria.
records.prior_reason: This continues the preceding family list with personal names; no individual identification follows from sharing those common names elsewhere.

records.text: From the sons of Esam: Mathani, Mathatha, Zabed, Eliphaleth, Ierami, Manasse and Semei.
records.prior_reason: The Esam family is not silently normalized to Asem in the earlier return list; the separately read family-name candidate remains unresolved.

records.text: From the sons of Bani: Moodi, Amram and Ouel;
records.prior_reason: The personal names under sons of Bani do not independently establish an earlier family or person identification; the list is preserved as written.

records.text: Banaia, Badaia and Chelia;
records.prior_reason: This list continuation provides personal names without distinguishing ancestry or events sufficient to identify them with other bearers.

records.text: Ouiechoa, Ieramoth and Eliasib;
records.prior_reason: These personal names in the continuing list do not securely identify the men with similarly named figures elsewhere.

records.text: Mathania, Mathanai; and acted
records.prior_reason: The unusual ending "and acted" and the named list continuation are preserved; no emendation or identification is imposed to manufacture a link.

records.text: the sons of Banoui and the sons of Semei,
records.prior_reason: The wording about sons of Banoui and sons of Semei follows the unusual preceding continuation; no reconstructed family boundary or personal equivalence is imposed.

records.text: and Selemia, Nathan and Adaia,
records.prior_reason: The continuing personal names lack independently verified distinguishing relationships, so common names are not treated as identities.

records.text: Machnadabou, Sesi and Sarou,
records.prior_reason: The unusual names in this continuation are preserved without spelling normalization or speculative personal identifications.

records.text: Ezerel, Selemia and Samaria,
records.prior_reason: The personal names are not identified with other similarly named men without independently distinguishing family or narrative evidence.

records.text: and Saloum, Amaria and Joseph.
records.prior_reason: The closing personal names of this continuation do not by themselves establish specific earlier identities.
